cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Hawaiian feathered war-god image (akua kaʻai/ʻaumakua type), constructed of wickerwork base with olona-cord netting, red and white feathers, pearl-shell eyes, and dog-teeth mouth — a well-documented Native Hawaiian ritual object form.

physical.title: figure
physical.summary:
Registration slip description by C H Read written in or after 1895:
War-god consisting of a grotesque crested head with elongated neck, made of wicker-work of ie-ie & overlaid with a fine netting of olona-cord covered with red feathers. The top & the sides of the crest are covered with white feathers spotted with occasional red feathers. The eyebrows which rise almost perpendicularly are of black feathers, the eyes being formed of long pointed ovals of pearl-shell with seed pupils. The distended mouth, the corners of which turn sharply upwards, is set with dogs' teeth: the interior is filled with featherwork, the feathers being in alternate red & white bands. The mouth appears to have been originally bordered with a double narrow band of black & yellow feathers. The ears seem to be indicated by small transverse bands of yellow feathers near the crest. The base of the neck also had a border of yellow feathers, only a few of which now remain.
